newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian minister calls for oil sharing contracts.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister calls for oil sharing contracts.

text.p: Finance minister Anthony Ani has renewed his call for oil production sharing contracts by Nigeria instead of the current joint ventures with multinational oil firms, the local Guardian newspaper reported on Monday.
The independent paper said Ani, speaking to reporters in the capital Abuja at the weekend, said Nigeria was dissatisfied with the joint ventures because it had no control over their operations.

"We don't even know how much it costs to explore and exploit, all that is happening is that we get bills which we have to settle," he said, adding "Nigerians are not actively involved in the business."

Under the current arrangements state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) has controlling shares in the joint ventures with Royal Dutch Shell group, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp, Agip SpA, Elf Aquitaine and Texaco Inc to explore and produce Nigerian crude oil.
Nigeria funds the joint ventures to the tune of its holding through a system of cash-calls and has often defaulted in paying promptly because of the huge amounts involved.
The oil companies have advised Nigeria to sell off its stake from the joint ventures to free itself from the burden of investing state funds in oil business.

In the last four years, however, the government has not entered into any joint ventures and has preferred to farm out blocks for exploration under production sharing contracts whereby the oil companies pay all the costs and recoup their investment if oil is found.

Ani, who in January said the contracts were a better system of exploiting Nigerian oil resources, said a scheme might be introduced whereby Nigeria would gradually withdraw from the joint ventures, the Guardian reported.
This could be replaced by a system providing for the oil companies to explore and exploit the oil and take their commission, he said.
